title: Thu 19 Nov · morning check
summary:
[b]Overnight:[/b] hawkish FOMC minutes (nearly all see more hikes, Waller open to 50bp); Australia lost 43.5k jobs, unemployment 4.9% (Aussie weakness condition met); French Senate passed the PLFSS but the spread widened to 156.3bp; VIX 24.56, back under 25.
[b]Next:[/b] APEC (Thu); US claims/Philly Fed 15:30; Japan CPI Fri 01:30; UK retail sales 09:00; Lagarde 10:30; Canada retail sales 15:30 (Bucharest).

USD.note: FOMC minutes: nearly all officials see more hikes as likely appropriate; Waller backs considering 50bp; December 25bp priced ~90–95%.

EUR.note: Senate adopted the PLFSS 201–124 (deficit €14bn vs €12.7bn); OAT–Bund widened to 156.3bp on 17 Nov; CMP 26 Nov.

GBP.note: No new BoE item; carried from CPI 3.6% below the BoE 3.7% projection (central +1, dovish R3 scenario still +1).

JPY.note: Katayama repeats US coordination and readiness to act (no action); BoJ December hike still expected; raw −0.9 held at 0.

CHF.note: VIX closed 24.56 on 18 Nov, back below the 25 trigger met on 17 Nov; HY spread 3.43%; regime re-measured on Friday.

CAD.note: Brent settled $91.95 (−1.3%), WTI $83.26 (−3.2%); no verified US–Canada deal; raw −4.5 held at −4.

AUD.note: October jobs −43.5k vs +25k, unemployment 4.9% vs 4.7%: weakness condition met; shadow +3 central, 0 if R2 turns −1.

NZD.note: No NZ release or RBNZ remark after T0.

XAU.note: Gold factor −3 unchanged; gold settled $3,728.80 (−3.5%), price context only; XAU shadow = G + USD shadow.

[b]Australia lost 43,500 jobs in October, and the stand-off is now leaning clearly toward the dollar.[/b]
Economists expected 25,000 new jobs; instead employment fell for a second month and unemployment jumped to 4.9%, the highest since late 2021. That meets the Aussie's written weakness condition. In the model, the jobs miss cancels the wage surprise, so the score holds at +3, but if the RBA outlook is cut to dovish the Aussie drops to 0. With the dollar at +6 after hawkish minutes, the read is −3, or −6.
